statement: We are the Creator. We created this game of experiences and entered it. Having designed it before entering, we cannot change its design from inside the game.
meaning: In Uday Kumar’s philosophy, God, the Creator, and the one Shakti point to the shared source appearing as every life. ‘We are the Creator’ refers to this common identity beyond our separate personalities. Remembering, choosing, learning, and caring all take place within the game’s unfolding; none places an individual outside it to rewrite the total design.
original: When none of this existed, there was only one energy (Brahman, Parabrahman, Ishwara, Paramatman, Allah, God, Yahweh). That energy is capable of creating anything. That energy is us. Back then, we were alone. Being alone, we decided to play a game and created this entire existence; this is the game of experiences. Having already decided how this game should unfold before stepping into it, we cannot make any changes midway.
steps: Bring the central statement to mind: we are the Creator who made and entered this game for experiences; we cannot rewrite its design from inside. Let this frame the situation you are about to examine.
Notice the scene and the role
Choose a small, ordinary event. What happened, what feeling arose, and which role feels caught in it? The experience is present; ask whether you have made that passing role your whole identity.
Notice the demand to control the game
What are you insisting must happen next? In this teaching, we cannot stand outside the game to replace its design. You do not know the next scene; notice what happens when you acknowledge that.

Recall that the other person is also an expression of the same Creator. Let that recognition inform the response that is needed in this scene. Speaking, listening, resting, or repairing a mistake are themselves experiences within the game.

Recall the whole statement again. Did identification with the role loosen? Did care arise more readily? Notice what changed or did not change; writing is not required. The aim is understanding that carries into life; repeating the words alone does not establish it.
practiceReflection: In this scene I became caught in the role of ___. I wanted the game to unfold as ___. Remembering the Creator within the already-designed game meant ___ to me. What I actually noticed was ___.

cases.title: When thoughts keep circling
cases.description: Remember the Creator while waiting for a scene you cannot dictate.
cases.connection: Within this philosophy, uncertainty is an experience in the game we entered. Remembering the Creator turns attention from demanding a particular next scene to noticing how the present one is being experienced.
cases.scene: You sent a message and no reply has arrived. The role of friend or partner feels rejected, and the mind keeps repeating, ‘They do not care about me.’
cases.remember: Recall the Creator who entered the game for experiences. Waiting and the fear of rejection belong to this scene; they do not describe the whole of who you are. The other person shares the same source. You cannot rewrite the game to demand an immediate reply, and you do not yet know why they have not answered.
cases.participation: A clear follow-up, or returning to the activity in front of you, can arise from this remembrance. Either is participation within the unfolding game. Notice whether your response expresses connection or an attempt to force the next scene.
cases.reflection: Which role feels rejected? What reply are you demanding from the game? Remember the shared Creator and the design you cannot rewrite from inside. What happens to the repeated story when you return to that understanding?

cases.title: When a conversation hurts
cases.description: See the same Creator in both roles within the disagreement.
cases.connection: If the same Creator appears in both people, disagreement takes place between roles within one game. This is the teaching’s basis for care arising through recognition, rather than through a separate command to behave well.
cases.scene: Someone interrupts you while you explain a concern. Anger appears and the role that wants respect begins to treat the other person as an enemy.
cases.remember: Both lives express the same Creator in this philosophy. The anger is an experience within the game; it need not become your whole identity. Remember that you cannot rewrite the total design or dictate another person’s response from outside it.
cases.participation: You might say, ‘I would like to finish, then I will listen.’ Pausing or leaving the conversation is also possible within the scene. Recognizing a shared source can inform a firm boundary; it does not erase the effects of the interruption or require staying where there is danger.
cases.reflection: Can you remember the Creator in both roles while feeling the anger? Which part of the next scene are you trying to dictate? From the understanding that your response also belongs to the game, what becomes clearer?

cases.title: When you judge yourself
cases.description: Distinguish a role’s mistake from the Creator experiencing that role.
cases.connection: The teaching locates identity in the Creator rather than in a successful or unsuccessful role. A mistake, the feeling about it, and learning afterwards are all experiences within the already-designed game.
cases.scene: You forgot to call when you said you would. Someone was inconvenienced. The thought changes from ‘I forgot’ to ‘I am a failure.’
cases.remember: Return to the Creator who entered this game. The missed call belongs to a changing role; it is not the whole of your identity. You cannot replace the scene that occurred or rewrite the total design. Remorse, understanding, and repair can also unfold within it.
cases.participation: Recognizing the same Creator in the person affected gives the apology its meaning. You may acknowledge the missed call and make a realistic arrangement. Let care for that connection guide the response, rather than treating punishment of yourself as the purpose of the scene.
cases.reflection: What label has the role taken on? Remember the Creator within the game whose design cannot be rewritten. Does that remembrance change how you meet the person affected, without denying what happened?

cases.title: When a decision feels difficult
cases.description: Make a choice within the game without claiming control of its design.
cases.connection: A fixed design does not remove decisions from experience. In this philosophy, weighing possibilities, deciding, and discovering the result are themselves parts of the game the Creator entered.
cases.scene: You are invited to help organize an event, but your week is full. You want to be useful and also want everyone to approve of you.
cases.remember: Notice the role seeking approval, then recall the Creator within the already-designed game. You cannot rewrite the whole to guarantee praise or a perfect result. You can examine the time available and what the invitation involves as part of your participation in this scene.
cases.participation: An honest offer of one hour, or a clear decline, may follow. The same Creator is present in the people involved, so their time and your existing commitments matter within the experience. The outcome unfolds; the decision does not put you outside the game.
cases.reflection: What outcome would you like to guarantee? Remember that the Creator is experiencing a decision inside a game whose design cannot be rewritten. What choice becomes clearer when approval no longer defines your identity?

cases.title: When possessions overshadow people
cases.description: Place a small part of creation beside the shared Creator in a relationship.
cases.connection: In Uday’s teaching, gold, diamonds, and money are small parts of the creation we entered. The Creator’s identity is not measured by possessing them. This is the proposed reason that relationships can regain importance as understanding deepens.
cases.example: An object becomes more important than a relationship
cases.scene: Someone close to you accidentally damages something valuable. Worry about its cost quickly becomes contempt for the person.
cases.remember: The object is one small part of creation; the other person is another expression of the same Creator. You cannot rewrite the game to undo this scene. The cost can still be addressed, but neither the object nor the loss contains your whole identity.
cases.participation: From that remembrance, a conversation about what happened and possible repair can unfold without reducing the relationship to the price of an object. Practical needs remain part of the game; this exercise is about attachment, not ignoring bills or giving away possessions.
cases.reflection: What has the object come to represent about your role or status? Remember the shared Creator within the fixed game. What changes when you consider the relationship alongside the loss?

cases.title: The movie and the lotus
cases.description: Experience a scene fully while remembering the Creator who entered it.
cases.connection: The movie analogy illustrates absorption and remembrance. The lotus image expresses the intended state of participation: within the pond of life, with such light attachment that it seems unclear whether its water touches you. Both point back to the Creator within the game.
cases.scene: In a movie theatre, a scene can bring laughter, tears, anger, or love. On leaving, remembering that it was a movie can change your relationship with those feelings. Think of a small event in your day that similarly absorbed you.
cases.remember: Uday applies that movement of remembrance to the game of experiences: we are the Creator who designed and entered it, and cannot rewrite the design from within. Return to that understanding while life continues. The lotus describes remaining in the experience without making each passing emotion your deepest identity.
cases.participation: Feel what is present and notice whether remembering the teaching changes your attachment to it. There is no required deadline for an emotion to leave. Remembrance means remaining engaged with life; it is not a demand to become numb or treat other people’s experiences as unreal.
cases.reflection: Which scene absorbed you? What does remembering the Creator and the game’s fixed design mean here? Can you allow the emotion while exploring the lotus image of being inwardly untouched? Describe what actually happens.
